playground.integrityMismatchNote: The file in the browser workspace no longer matches the source you supplied. Do not trust anything this session reports; load the script again.
playground.integrityNote: SHA-256 of the file actually executed in the browser workspace, compared byte for byte with the source you supplied. It catches a script or the engine modifying the source unintentionally. It is not a defence against a script written to defeat it, which runs in the same interpreter as your figure.
playground.integrityUnavailableNote: This browser could not compute the hash, so the comparison never ran — which is why this does not claim the file is unchanged.
playground.landingSubtitle: Every example here is an ordinary Matplotlib script. It runs — and you edit it — entirely in your browser.

playground.uploadNote: For single-file scripts only — nothing that relies on local data, sibling modules or other local resources.
playground.uploadScopeBad: Doesn’t work: reading local files (pd.read_csv("data.csv"), np.load(...), open(...)); sibling modules; local images or fonts; project-relative paths; full Conda projects.
playground.uploadScopeGood: Works: one UTF-8 .py file; NumPy, Matplotlib and the packages pinned in this runtime; data written in the script or generated by code.

relink.descDoc: This layout references files that do not exist in the current figure library (common when opening a project package on another machine). Pick a replacement for each; panels you leave alone stay missing and will be flagged by the pre-export check.
relink.descPaste: Panels on the clipboard reference files that do not exist in the current figure library. Pick a replacement for each, or skip that panel.
relink.footnote: Relinking resets the figure edits to the new asset's size and script (overrides are bound to elements of the original script, so they do not transfer reliably). Position, size, stacking order and grouping are kept.
relink.titleDoc: Panels in this document are missing assets
relink.titlePaste: The pasted panels are missing assets

about.diagnosticsHintBefore: When something goes wrong, export a zip and send it to us: it contains the version, your platform, the rendering interpreter, AI CLI detection results and recent logs.
about.diagnosticsHintStrong: Keys and your home directory are redacted automatically
about.privacy: All data and rendering stay on this machine; nothing is uploaded. The assistant runs the Codex / Claude command-line tools installed locally. There are only two outbound requests: the update check (which you can turn off under “Updates”) and the anonymous usage statistics below, which stay off until you explicitly opt in.
about.tagline: Figure layout and parameterized chart editing for papers

canvas.companionsExplain: Companion elements are titles, axis labels and legends you have positioned by hand, plus colorbar axes and twinx twins. They are either pinned to figure coordinates or are sibling axes, so without this they stay behind when the axes move. Turn it off to move only the axes themselves.
